events.credibility_reason: Announcement only; no written argument ever located, paper still 'in preparation'. Apex cubic graphs alone are not a subclass of the P-minor-free class, so it is a reduction component rather than a settled case.
Announced complete proof of the cubic case never published as a whole; apex part unwritten.

Single-version 'draft-paper' claiming a landmark (non-computer proof of Tait/Tutte), title claim not supported by the abstract's hedged 'applicability' wording, no uptake in 21 years, field still treats the cubic case as resting on RSST and the 2026 apex work.
Withdrawn (arXiv v2, 7 Oct 2020); results said to be previously obtained by Kochol.

Completes the cubic case only via the RSST reduction whose full proof is described as unpublished; computer-assisted lemmas not independently checked; seven weeks without engagement. Established authors, no identified error.

why: The statement asks about all bridgeless P-minor-free graphs, so every result on a subclass (P10-, P/3-, P/e-minor-free, or the cubic case) is a case. Pintér 2026 settles the proper subclass of P/e-minor-free graphs; Inoue et al. 2026 claim the cubic case by supplying the apex half of the RSST reduction. Both are unreviewed preprints. Apex-only and doublecross-only results are reduction components on classes not contained in the P-minor-free class, so they are variants; the RSST structural papers and reduction are none; Kochol's 5-flow, the matroid result and the projective-planar/toroidal papers are variants. AI: Pintér's ChatGPT/Claude disclosure is literature research, editing and help writing verification code; Inoue's Copilot helped implement verification software. Neither produced mathematics in the result, so both are none.
doubts: Classing the Inoue 2026 apex result as a case of the statement depends on the RSST reduction being sound. The authors' 'finally proves' claim covers the cubic case, but the full reduction is reported as unpublished. Whether Pintér's verifier code counts as mathematics was a close call: the disclosure says only 'help writing the accompanying code', and the author verified it, so I read it as coding assistance.
